docs.title: readall.py
docs.text: This script handles automated multi-channel acquisition using NI-DAQmx and logs data to CSV.

docs.title: === IMPORTS ===
docs.text: import nidaqmx from nidaqmx.constants import AcquisitionType from nidaqmx.stream_readers import AnalogMultiChannelReader import numpy as np import csv import time

docs.title: Define total duration of the test and sampling rate
docs.text: duration = 10 # seconds sampling_rate = 1000 # samples per second channel_range = (-10.0, 10.0) # input voltage range

docs.title: Automatically detect all analog input channels on Dev1 and add them to
docs.text:
the task task = nidaqmx.Task() device = nidaqmx.system.Device("Dev1")

for channel in device.ai_physical_chans.channel_names: task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan(channel, min_val=channel_range[0], max_val=channel_range[1])

docs.title: Set the task to acquire continuously at defined sample rate
Preallocate memory space to hold incoming data
docs.text: num_channels = len(device.ai_physical_chans.channel_names) samples_per_read = int(sampling_rate * duration / 10) # Adjust per loop buffer = np.zeros((num_channels, samples_per_read), dtype=np.float64)

docs.title: === START TASK AND READ LOOP ===
docs.text:
task.start() start_time = time.time()

with open("readout.csv", "w", newline="") as csvfile: writer = csv.writer(csvfile)

while time.time() - start_time < duration:
    reader.read_many_sample(buffer,

number_of_samples_per_channel=samples_per_read, timeout=5.0)

    # Transpose and write each row to the CSV file
    for row in buffer.T:
        writer.writerow(row)

task.stop() task.close()

docs.title: A CSV file called "readout.csv" will be created with one row per sample.
Each column in the CSV represents one channel's reading at that time

docs.text:
# setupDAQ.py # This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in Python. # It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition, # and how the DAQ system starts and stops.

This script sets up a Data Acquisition (DAQ) task using NI-DAQmx in Python. It defines which channels to use, the timing of the acquisition, and how the DAQ system starts and stops.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
import nidaqmx

Import the NI-DAQmx Python library.

task = nidaqmx.Task()

Create a new task object to manage DAQ operations.

docs.title: Channel Configuration
docs.text:
task.ai_channels.add_ai_voltage_chan("Dev1/ai0", min_val=-10.0, max_val=10.0)

Add AI0 channel on Dev1 with ±10V input range.

docs.title: Clock and Sampling Rate
docs.text:
task.timing.cfg_samp_clk_timing( rate=1000, sample_mode=nidaqmx.constants.AcquisitionType.CONTINUOUS )

Configure the sample clock for continuous acquisition at 1000 Hz.

docs.title: Task Execution
docs.text:
task.start()

Start the task to begin acquisition.

# Insert acquisition logic here (e.g., read buffer, log data)

task.stop()

Stop the task after acquisition is complete.

task.close()

Close the task to release hardware and clean up resources.

docs.text:
